title: Add batched event delivery preserving FSEvents callback boundaries
description: FileSystemEventStream.swift:48-52 loops and calls eventHandler(event) per-event, discarding the FSEvents batch boundary. FSEvents naturally coalesces related events (e.g. atomic save = created+modified+renamed). Yield [FolderContentChangeEvent] to preserve this semantic grouping, matching Panda's approach. The existing per-event API can flatten batches for backward compatibility.

comments.author: Beads
comments.text:
Composes cleanly with the 2.1.0 StreamCondition work: yielding [FolderContentChangeEvent] per callback preserves the interleaving of conditions and file changes exactly as FSEvents produced it, which is required - a change reported after a MustScanSubDirs survives the rescan it demands, one before it does not. No separate channel for conditions.

Still open (Q3): does the batched form replace the per-event API or sit beside it as makeBatchedStream? Cheaper to answer once asyncfilemonitor-as7 has deleted the instance API and halved the factory matrix.

title: Nest FileSystemEventStreamError as FileSystemEventStream.Error
description: FileSystemEventStreamError (FileSystemEventStream.swift:16-21) is a top-level type but only thrown by FileSystemEventStream.make(). Nest it as FileSystemEventStream.Error for clearer ownership.
close_reason: Nested as FileSystemEventStream.Error; it is now internal along with its enclosing type

title: Let callers choose directory-level instead of file-level events
description: FileSystemEventStream.make always sets kFSEventStreamCreateFlagFileEvents, so every consumer pays for per-file events. A consumer that only needs to know 'something under this folder changed' would get far fewer events without the flag. Expose a granularity option (directory or file) on both makeStream forms, defaulting to file so existing behaviour is unchanged.

title: Move EventHandlerBox inside FileSystemEventStream.make()
description: EventHandlerBox (FileSystemEventStream.swift:28-34) is defined at file scope but only used inside make(). Move it to be a function-local class, matching Panda's pattern of scoping types to exactly where they're needed.
close_reason: Nested in FileSystemEventStream rather than function-local: the C callback also references EventHandlerBox, so both had to move together

title: Delete the multicast instance API in 3.0
description:
FolderContentMonitor's instance form (init + makeStream()) exists to let several subscribers share one FSEventStream. No consumer uses it that way: TheArchive2, the only consumer, calls makeStream() exactly once per monitor. Deleting it removes MulticastAsyncStream, StreamLifecycleEvent, the Mutex state machine and the lifecycle task, and lets every feature below be designed once instead of twice.

Decided without a deprecation cycle: 2.0.0 is a day old and the sole consumer is in-house.

Two further reasons it blocks other work. (1) On the instance path FileSystemEventStream.make runs inside the lifecycle task on first-subscriber, so there is no caller left to throw to - a throwing factory (asyncfilemonitor-xo0) cannot work there. (2) That same asynchrony means monitoring starts some time after init returns, which reopens the buffering window TheArchive2's CollectionFolderMonitor relies on being closed; the static form creates the stream synchronously in the AsyncStream build closure.

Migration for TheArchive2 is constructor + makeStream() -> FolderContentMonitor.makeStream(url:).

title: Fix silent error handling: finish continuations on FSEventStream creation failure
description: FolderContentMonitor.swift:175 just print()s when FileSystemEventStream.make() fails. Consumers get a stream that never yields and never finishes. Should call continuation.finish() (or a new finishAll() on MulticastAsyncStream) so the for-await loop ends cleanly, matching Panda's pattern.
close_reason: Both paths now finish continuations on FSEventStream creation failure

comments.author: Beads
comments.text: Half-done on main: the static makeStream path now finishes continuations on failure. The instance path still only print()s at Sources/AsyncFileMonitor/FolderContentMonitor.swift:175. Note the stashed static-makeStream slice satisfies finish() but swallows the error entirely, so consumers still cannot distinguish 'no changes' from 'failed to start' - consider an AsyncThrowingStream variant.

title: Pass kFSEventStreamCreateFlagWatchRoot so rootChanged can fire
description:
StreamCondition.rootChanged is named but unreachable: the Core Services headers state it is only ever delivered when the stream was created with kFSEventStreamCreateFlagWatchRoot, and FileSystemEventStream.make passes only UseCFTypes | FileEvents. So 'a directory along the path to the watched folder changed, and the watched path may no longer exist' is currently unobservable.

Sibling of asyncfilemonitor-nav and asyncfilemonitor-9cr: all three are creation-flag/configuration options on the same factories, so settle their shape (loose parameters vs a config struct) together. Default off to keep current behaviour.

title: Let callers choose the event delivery queue's QoS
description: FileSystemEventStream.make hardcodes DispatchQueue(label: "FileSystemEventStream", qos: .userInteractive). That suits a UI observing a folder the user is looking at, but a background indexer or sync process would reasonably want a lower QoS so event delivery does not compete with foreground work. Expose qos as a parameter on both makeStream forms, defaulting to .userInteractive so existing behaviour is unchanged.

title: Surface FSEventStream creation failure to consumers instead of print()
description: Both makeStream paths now finish() the stream when FileSystemEventStream.make() fails (asyncfilemonitor-dee), but the error itself only reaches a print(). Consumers still cannot distinguish 'watched folder had no changes' from 'monitoring never started'. Consider an AsyncThrowingStream variant, or a throwing factory, so the failure is part of the API rather than a log line.

comments.author: Beads
comments.text: Consumer demand registered from TheArchive2 (ta2-coder), which adopted 2.0.0 with no call-site changes. They journal when the event stream finishes without their own teardown having cancelled it, so a collection whose FSEventStream never started now leaves a trace instead of silently losing external-change monitoring. That distinguishes 'died' from 'torn down' but not why it died. What they want: a typed reason on stream finish, or an error event, so the journal line can name the failure. No urgency stated. Panda's FolderMonitor.makeEventStream is a reference point for the minimum bar - it calls log.error on setup failure where we print().

comments.author: Beads
comments.text:
Design resolved in planning; blocked on asyncfilemonitor-as7.

Two distinct failure modes were conflated here. Mid-stream degradation (FSEvents dropping events) shipped in 2.1.0 as StreamCondition - see docs/FSEvents Flag Reference.md. This issue is now only about STARTUP failure: create/start fails and monitoring never begins.

Recommended shape: a throwing factory returning a plain AsyncStream. Not AsyncThrowingStream, not an error-as-element case.

Why it works: FSEvents can only fail at create/start, never mid-stream via the callback, and AsyncStream's build closure runs synchronously at construction (verified). So the failure is available on the caller's thread at the call site. Build it with AsyncStream.makeStream() rather than the trailing-closure init, which cannot rethrow.

This satisfies TheArchive2's recorded demand better than a typed finish reason: if construction succeeded, the stream can only finish through consumer teardown, so 'died' vs 'torn down' stops being ambiguous by construction. Cost to them: CollectionFolderMonitor.init is non-throwing today and would need to throw or catch.

title: Share one FSEventStream per path across the process
description:
Parked idea raised while deciding the fate of the instance API. Today two observers of the same folder create two kernel streams, coalesced independently, so their event IDs and batch boundaries differ. A path-keyed registry would give one stream per path per process: fewer kernel resources, and identical events for all observers of a path.

This is what the multicast machinery would actually be good for - note the instance API does NOT do it today (each instance owns its own stream). Deliberately not a reason to keep the instance API; revisit after 3.0. Changes observable semantics, so it needs its own design pass.

title: Make MulticastAsyncStream, StreamLifecycleEvent, and FileSystemEventStreamError internal
description: These types are implementation details never used by consumers. Making them internal cleans up the public API surface. Currently public at: MulticastAsyncStream.swift:43, MulticastAsyncStream.swift:22, FileSystemEventStream.swift:16.
close_reason: MulticastAsyncStream, StreamLifecycleEvent and the stream error are internal; docc topics updated
